Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:10:1.hebrew: דמקרבי כלים לגבי כותל - טובא, דליכא תחלתו בפשיעה, דאי הוו קפצי, לברא ממאני הוו קפצי, וכי נפול להדי כותל ואיתביר מנא, אנוס הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:10:1.english: Where the vessels were brought close to the wall - Very [close], such that there is no beginning with negligence; for if [the animals] had jumped, they would have jumped beyond the vessels, and when they fell directly alongside the wall and a vessel broke, it is [an unavoidable] accident.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:11:1.hebrew: שאפילו נפלו חייבין - ואפילו למ"ד תחלתו בפשיעה וסופו באונס פטור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:11:1.english: That even [if] they fell, they are liable - And even according to the one who says [that a case whose] beginning is with negligence and whose end is through unavoidable accident is exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:11:2.hebrew: משכחת לה בכותל רעוע - שמעקה הגג רעוע, דאפילו לגבי נפילה הוי פשיעה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:11:2.english: You find it in [the case of] an unstable wall - For the parapet of the roof is unstable, such that even with respect to falling it is [considered] negligence.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:11:3.english: Because he should have brought [it to mind] - [This is] a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:11:4.hebrew: לא נפל ארחי ונפול אינהו כו' - כלומר, כיון דסוף סוף לא נפל ארחי, אין סופו בפשיעה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:11:4.english: No bricks fell and they [the animals] fell, etc. - That is to say, since ultimately no bricks fell, its end is not through negligence.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:11:5.hebrew: בכותל צר - שמעקה הגג צר ודחוק, וכי הניחם בראש הגג הוה ליה לאסוקי אדעתיה דקפצי אמעקה כדרכן (ומן המעקה שהוא צר נפלי). לישנא אחרינא: צר — משופע:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:11:5.english: With a narrow wall - For the parapet of the roof is narrow and cramped, and when he left them on top of the roof, it should have occurred to him that they jump onto the parapet in their usual manner (and from the parapet, which is narrow, they fall). Another explanation: "narrow" [means] sloped.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:12:1.hebrew: מלמטה למעלה פטורין - מנזק שלם, וחייב בחצי נזק, דמשונין הן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:12:1.english: From below to above they are exempt - [Exempt] from full damages, and [the owner is] liable for half-damages, because they are unusual.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:12:2.hebrew: אדם ותרנגול כו' - אדם, אי נמי לאו אורחיה לקפוץ מלמטה למעלה, חייב, דאין באדם צד תמות אלא בבהמה. ותרנגול, דרכו לדלג אפילו מלמטה למעלה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:12:2.english: A person or a chicken, etc. - A person, even if it is not his usual manner to jump from below to above, is liable, for there is no aspect of innocuousness [tamut] for a person, only for an animal. And [as for] a chicken, it is its usual manner to jump even from below to above.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:1:1.hebrew: בעלמא בור ברשותו פטור - דלא חייבה תורה אלא על בור ברה"ר, וכדיליף רבי ישמעאל טעמיה התם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:1:1.english: Usually, a pit within his [own] property [is] exempt - For the Torah only imposed liability for a pit in the public domain, as Rabbi Yishmael derives his reason there.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:2:1.hebrew: בעלמא בור ברשותו חייב - הואיל והפקירו. והכא, מ"ט בהמה שאכלתן חייבת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:2:1.english: Usually, a pit in his property is liable - Since he declared it ownerless. And here, what is the reason [that] an animal that ate them is liable?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:2:2.hebrew: דבשלמא בור איכא למימר לאו אדעתיה - דשור לנטורי נפשיה מבור, וכיון דברשות נכנס — דהא הפקיר רשותו — חייב בעל הבור. אבל פירות כו':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:2:2.english: Granted, [with regard to] a pit, it is possible to say [that] it is not on [its] mind - [that is, the mind] of the ox to guard itself from a pit; and since it entered with permission — for [the owner] declared his property ownerless — the owner of the pit is liable. However, [with regard to] produce, etc.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:2:3.hebrew: הא קא חזי להו - ואפילו הוחלקה בהן, פטור; ואע"ג דכל תקלה בור הוא, הנ"מ ברה"ר, דאין לו רשות לתת שם תקלה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:2:3.english: Behold, it sees them - And even if [the animal] slipped on them, [the owner] is exempt; and even though any obstacle [is considered] a pit, that applies [only] in the public domain, where he has no permission to place an obstacle there.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:4:1.hebrew: ר' יוסי היינו ת"ק - דקס"ד דלאו אתוך הרחבה קאי רבי יוסי דלבעי לחיוביה, דהא כתיב "ובער בשדה אחר" ולא ברה"ר; אלא אצידי רחבה קאי, דאין דרכה לאכול אלא להלך, וזו שאכלה חייבת. הלכך, היינו ת"ק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:4:1.english: Rabbi Yosei is [the same as] the first tanna - For we initially assumed that Rabbi Yosei is not referring to the middle of the public square so as to want to hold him liable, since it is written: "and it shall feed in another's field," and not in the public domain; rather, he is referring to the sides of the public square, where it is not its normal way to eat, only to walk, and this one that ate is liable. Therefore, he is [the same as] the first tanna.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:4:2.hebrew: מחזרת איכא בינייהו - דשמעינן לר"מ דאמר בצידי הרחבה משלמת מה שהזיקה, וכגון דאזלה וקמה בצידי רחבה, אבל מחזרת לא. וקאמר רבי יוסי: אין דרכה להחזיר ראשה ולאכול אלא להלך, וזו שהחזירה ואכלה חייבת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:4:2.english: [An animal that] turns [its head] is [the difference] between them - For we heard [regarding] Rabbi Meir that he said [that] on the sides of the public square it pays for what it damaged — such as where it went and stood on the sides of [the] public square — but [when it] turns [its head], [it does] not. And Rabbi Yosei says: It is not its way to turn its head and eat, rather to walk; and [therefore] this [animal] that turned [its head] and ate is liable.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:5:1.english: And here they disagree about “it consumed in the field of another” - And even for [eating in] the midst of the plaza, Rabbi Yosei holds him liable.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:5:2.hebrew: ולא ברשות המזיק - שאם הכניס פירותיו לחצר בעל הבית שלא ברשות, ואכלתן בהמתו של בעל הבית, פטור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:5:2.english: And not in the domain of the damager - For if [someone] brought his produce into a homeowner's courtyard without permission, and the homeowner's animal ate it, [the homeowner] is exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:6:1.english: Let him say to him, "What are you doing in my domain?" - And why do I need a verse [to teach this]?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:6:2.hebrew: דאילפא ורבי אושעיא - דאמר אילפא לעיל: בהמה שפשטה צוארה ואכלה מעל גבי חבירתה, חייבת. ודר' אושעיא, דאמר: בהמה הקופצת ואכלה מתוך הקופה, חייבת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:6:2.english: [That] of Ilfa and Rabbi Oshaya - For Ilfa said above: An animal that stretched out its neck and ate from the back of another [animal] is liable. And [that] of Rabbi Oshaya, who said: An animal that jumps and eats from inside a basket is liable.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:6:3.hebrew: איכא בינייהו - ר"מ סבר: מתוך הרחבה לעולם פטור, אלא לפי מה שנהנית, ואפילו בדאילפא ור' אושעיא. ואתא רבי יוסי למימר: אין דרכה לפשוט צוארה על חבירתה, ואין דרכה לקפוץ מדרך ולאכול, אלא להלך, ואית ליה דאילפא ודרבי אושעיא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:6:3.english: [The difference] between them is - Rabbi Meir holds: [When an animal eats] from the public thoroughfare, [the owner] is always exempt [from full damages, paying] only according to what it benefited, even in [the cases of] Ilfa and Rabbi Oshaya. And Rabbi Yosei comes to say: It is not its normal way to stretch its neck onto its fellow [animal], and it is not its normal way to jump from the road and eat — rather, [its normal way is] to walk [and eat] — and [thus] he holds [in accordance with] Ilfa and Rabbi Oshaya.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:7:1.hebrew: מפני שהן מועדין - לקפוץ. וברשות הניזק קאמר, דתולדה דרגל היא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:7:1.english: Because they are forewarned - to jump. And [the Mishnah] is speaking of [damage occurring] in the domain of the injured party, for it is a subcategory of Foot.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:7:2.english: For the cake, he pays full damage - For it is [a case of] Tooth in the domain of the injured party.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:7:3.hebrew: ועל הגדיש חצי נזק - מפרש בגמ':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:7:3.english: And for the stack [of grain], half damages - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:8:1.hebrew: תחלתו בפשיעה - דאיבעי לאסוקי אדעתיה דלמא קפצי, דהא אורחייהו לקפוץ:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:8:1.english: Its beginning [is] with negligence - For he should have considered that perhaps they would jump, since it is their way to jump.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:9:1.hebrew: הניחא למ"ד כו' - אמוראי פליגי בה בפרק [המפקיד] (ב"מ ד' מב.):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:9:1.english: This works out well according to the one who says, etc. - Amoraim dispute it in the chapter [entitled] Hamafkid (Bava Metzia 42a).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:9:2.hebrew: וסופו באונס - דהא נפלו, ונפילה לא הוה ליה לאסוקי אדעתיה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 21b:9:2.english: And ends in an accident - For they fell, and falling was not [something] he had to anticipate.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 21b:12:1.hebrew: אדם ותרנגול כו' - וא"ת: ומה חידוש באדם דחייב? וי"ל: דנפקא מינה אם הפקיד ביתו לחבירו לשמור ויש שם חש"ו, שיש לו ליזהר שלא ידלגו מלמטה למעלה וישברו כלים. [ואומר ר"י]: מתוך כך נראה לפרש דהא דקתני "הכלב והגדי שדלגו מלמטה למעלה פטורין" — דהיינו לגמרי, דחשיב אונס; להכי איצטריך לאשמועינן באדם דחייב. דאי פטורין מנ"ש וחייבין ח"נ, ואינו אלא משנה בעלמא, אמאי אצטריך לאשמועינן באדם דחייב? ואתי שפיר הא דמסיק "ומאי פטורין", ואית דגרסי "אי הכי אמאי פטורין"; דמעיקרא ניחא ליה "פטורין", דס"ד פטורין לגמרי קאמר מלמעלה למטה כמו מלמטה למעלה, דלאו אורחיה למיקפץ כלל, אבל כיון דמוקי בדאפיך מיפך, דאינו אלא משונה בעלמא, אמאי פטורין? ונראה דגם לפי המסקנא מלמטה למעלה פטורין לגמרי, דאנוס הוא — דלמה יחזור מסברא ראשונה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 21b:12:1.english: A person or a chicken, etc. - And if you say: What is the novelty regarding a person that he is liable? One can say that the practical difference is if someone entrusted his house to his fellow to guard, and there are deaf-mutes, imbeciles, or minors there, [teaching] that he must take care that they do not jump from below to above and break vessels. [And Ri says:] Accordingly, it seems [correct] to explain that this which [the baraita] teaches, "If a dog or a goat jumped from below to above, they are exempt," means completely [exempt], because it is considered an unavoidable accident; therefore, it was necessary to teach us regarding a person that he is liable. For if they were [only] exempt from full damage and liable for half damage, and it were merely atypical, why would it be necessary to teach us regarding a person that he is liable? And this fits well with what [the Gemara] concludes: "And what [does] 'exempt' [mean]?" — and there are those who read: "If so, why are they exempt?" — for initially, "exempt" was understandable to [the Gemara], because it thought [the baraita] meant completely exempt, from above to below just like from below to above, since it is not their way to jump at all; however, once [Rav Pappa] establishes it as a case where they reversed [their manner of jumping], which is merely atypical, why are they exempt? And it seems that even according to the conclusion, [when jumping] from below to above they are completely exempt, for it is an unavoidable accident — for why would [the Gemara] retract its initial reasoning?

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 21b:5:1.hebrew: אי כרב אי כשמואל - רבי יוסי לא מצי סבר כשמואל, דהא מחייב ברה"ר, אלא כלומר: אי כרב, דחשיב חצר הניזק, אי כשמואל, דחשיב ליה רה"ר — אע"ג דלר' יוסי אין נפקותא. ולפי' הקונטרס ניחא טפי: אי כרב, דחשיב ליה קרן, אי כשמואל, דחשיב ליה שן:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 21b:5:1.english: Either like Rav or like Shmuel - Rabbi Yosei cannot hold like Shmuel [to exempt him], for [Rabbi Yosei] holds one liable in the public domain; rather, it means: either like Rav, who considers [it] the damaged party's courtyard, or like Shmuel, who considers it the public domain — even though for Rabbi Yosei there is no practical difference [between the two]. And according to Rashi's explanation it fits even better: either like Rav, who considers it keren [horn], or like Shmuel, who considers it shen [tooth].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 21b:5:2.hebrew: ומר סבר - פי' ר"א: "ובער בשדה אחר" — ולא בשדה המזיק, אבל ברה"ר חייב. וא"ת: דהא לעיל (בבא קמא יח.) אמר דר"א ס"ל כרבי טרפון, ועל כרחך מקרן ברה"ר מייתי לה, וא"כ שן ורגל פטור ברה"ר? וי"ל, דלעיל מיירי לפי המסקנא דהכא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 21b:5:2.english: And [one] Sage holds - Explanation: [This refers to] Rabbi Elazar: "And it consumed in the field of another" — and not in the field of the one responsible for the damage, but in the public domain he is liable. And if you ask: For earlier (Bava Kamma 18a) [the Gemara] stated that Rabbi Elazar holds like Rabbi Tarfon, and perforce he derives it from Horn in the public domain, and if so, Tooth and Foot are exempt in the public domain? One can answer that earlier [the Gemara] is speaking according to the conclusion here:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 21b:6:1.hebrew: דאילפא ורבי אושעיא - לאו מענין אחד, דרבי אושעיא מיירי בקופצת דהוי קרן, ואילפא איירי על גבי חבירתה דחשיב שן:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 21b:6:1.english: [The cases] of Ilfa and Rabbi Oshaya - [They are] not of the same subject; for Rabbi Oshaya is speaking of [an animal] jumping, which is [classified as] keren [Horn], whereas Ilfa is speaking of [an animal eating from] on the back of another [animal], which is considered shen [Tooth].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 21b:8:1.hebrew: הא נפלו פטורין אלמא קסבר כו' - וא"ת: היכי דמי? אי מקרבי כלים לגבי כותל — היכי מיתברי בקפיצה, והא אמרינן בסמוך דכי קפצי מאבראי קפצי? ואי מרחקי — היכי משתברי בנפילה? וי"ל: כגון שהיו לא מרוחקות ולא מקורבות, דמיתברי בין בנפילה בין בקפיצה. אי נמי: בכלי ארוך, דאי נפלי — לצד הסמוך לכותל מיתבר, ואי קפצי — מיתבר לצד המרוחק:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 21b:8:1.english: "If they fell, they are exempt; apparently he holds, etc." - And if you ask: What is the case? If the vessels are close to the wall — how do they break by jumping, when we say shortly [in the Gemara] that when they jump, they jump from the outside [i.e., further away from the wall]? And if they are far [from the wall] — how do they break by falling? One can answer: For example, where they were neither far nor close, so that they break both by falling and by jumping. Alternatively, [it refers] to a long vessel, such that if they fall, it breaks on the side close to the wall, and if they jump, it breaks on the side that is far [from the wall].
